title: Annotatio I §.III vs Musaeus: Eucharistic bread still abstract; body of composite; synecdoche / improper
pass_a_gloss: If you press with Johannes Musaeus’s peculiar disputation on the Sacred Supper opposed to Vorstius §. 99 — In the Sacramental proposition a Concrete is also in its way predicated of a Concrete, so that it is not said: the nature of this bread is the nature of Christ’s body, but only, this bread, namely Eucharistic, blessed bread, not common bread, but the Eucharist, consisting of two things, earthly and heavenly, is Christ’s body, citing Bajer Disp. on Impanation §.30 — besides that (1) he partly leaves the bread to be an abstract nature, inasmuch as merely Eucharistic or blessed and no longer common it by no means deserts its abstract nature or yields into a concrete: For bread (an abstract nature) does not by being blessed and separated by blessing from common use exchange abstract nature with concrete — otherwise every abstract thing separated by a peculiar blessing from common use would by that very fact be converted into a concrete; partly he confounds Eucharistic bread with the Eucharist, of which latter you may rightly say it consists of two things, earthly and heavenly, not likewise of the former except from a hypothesis assumed and not yet proved; also (2) it still remains that nonetheless the abstract nature of Christ’s body, or the abstract body of Christ, is predicated of the concrete, or of the composite of body and bread, and so this sacramental predication is unlike personal propositions (in which a concrete, not an abstract, is predicated of a Concrete). But when an abstract is predicated directly of a Concrete, as still a disparate of a disparate is predicated, so the predication cannot but be improper: for thus a part is predicated of a whole, and by this reason the predication is made synechdochic, consequently tropical or improper.
pass_b_english: Musaeus (§.99 vs Vorstius) claims the sacramental line somehow predicates concrete of concrete — this Eucharistic bread / Eucharist of two things is Christ’s body — citing Bajer on Impanation.
But blessing does not turn bread’s abstract nature into a concrete; and he conflates Eucharistic bread with the Eucharist itself.

Even then an abstract body is still predicated of a composite of body and bread — unlike personal propositions — so abstract of concrete remains disparate of disparate, a synecdoche, and thus improper.
source_text: Si instes cum Johanne Museo disp. peculiari de S. Coena, Vorstio oppositâ §. 99: In Sacramentali propositione etiam suo modo praedicari Concretum de Concreto, ita ut non dicatur: natura hujus panis est natura corporis Christi, sed tantùm, hic panis, scil. Eucharisticus, panis benedictus, non panis communis, sed Eucharistia, ex duabus rebus, terrena & caelesti, constans, est corpus Christi, citante Bajero Disp. de impanatione §.30., praeterquam quod (1) panem partim naturam abstractam relinquit esse, quatenus nempe Eucharisticus seu benedictus tantùm, nec communis ampliùs, per hoc, abstractam suam naturam nequaquam deserit, vel in concretam concedit: Neque enim panis (natura abstracta) per id, quòd ei benedictum & per benedictionem à communi usu separatus est, naturam abstractam cum concreta commutât, omni alioquin re abstractâ, & per benedictionem peculiarem à communi usu separata, per hoc ipsum in concretam convertenda; partim Eucharisticum panem, cum Eucharistia, confundit, de quorum posteriori rectè quidem dicas, ex duabus rebus, terrena & caelesti, constare, non item de priori, nisi ex sumta, nec adhuc dum probata, hypothesi, etiam (2) remanet adhuc, abstractam nihilominus naturam corporis Christi, seu abstractum corpus Christi, de concreto, seu de composito ex corpore & pane, praedicari, eòque personalibus propositionibus, (in quibus concretum, non verò abstractum, de Concreto praedicatur) praedicationem hanc sacramentalem dissimilem esse. Quando verò abstractum de Concreto directè praedicatur, uti adhucdum disparatum de disparato praedicatur, ita praedicatio non potest non esse impropria: praedicatur enim sic pars de toto, hacque ratione praedicatio conficitur synechdochica, per consequens, tropica seu impropria.
